candidate_invariant.name: SIGN_FLIP_TRANSLATION_SYMMETRY_GROUP
candidate_invariant.definition: H(F) is the subgroup of GF(2)^n consisting of variable-bit flip masks h such that complementing the sign of every occurrence of each variable with h_i=1 maps the clause multiset F to itself.

polynomial_computation.support_partition: Group clauses by their underlying variable support S. For width<=3, each support has at most 2^3=8 possible literal-sign patterns.
polynomial_computation.local_stabilizer: For each support S, enumerate the at most 8 masks a in GF(2)^S and keep exactly those translating the sign-pattern multiset on S to itself. This stabilizer is a subgroup/linear subspace of GF(2)^S.
polynomial_computation.global_group: Translate each local subspace condition into linear equations over GF(2) and solve their intersection by Gaussian elimination. Hence a basis of H(F) and r(F) are computable in deterministic polynomial time.

exact_safe_descent_theorem.statement: If r(F)>0, then r(F) independent pivot variables can be fixed to 0 simultaneously while preserving satisfiability exactly.
proof: Row-reduce a basis of H(F) so the r pivot coordinates form an identity matrix.
If alpha satisfies F and has pivot-bit vector b, xor alpha with the unique basis combination h whose pivot coordinates equal b.
Because h is a formula sign-flip symmetry, alpha xor h is also a model of F.
Its pivot bits are all 0. Therefore F is SAT iff the simplified restriction F[pivots=0] is SAT.
exact_safe_descent_theorem.transition_cost: Polynomial: compute H(F), row-reduce, assign pivots, simplify clauses.
exact_safe_descent_theorem.strict_progress: When r(F)>0 at least one variable is removed without branching and without SAT-oracle use.

obstruction.statement: The invariant is not universal because arbitrarily large SAT and UNSAT formulas can have H(F)={0}.
obstruction.SAT_family: F_n={x1, (not x1 or x2), ..., (not x_{n-1} or x_n)} has the unique model x1=...=xn=1. Any nonzero flip symmetry would map that unique model to a distinct model, impossible; hence H(F_n)={0}.
obstruction.UNSAT_family: U_n={x1, (not x1 or x2), ..., (not x_{n-1} or x_n), not x_n}. The positive unit clause forces h_1=0 for any sign-flip symmetry; each binary implication support then forces h_i=h_{i+1}; hence all h_i=0. Thus H(U_n)={0} while U_n is UNSAT.

next_admissible_math.question: Can another polynomially computable exact quotient/descent invariant act on the symmetry-rigid hard core H(F)={0}, without reverting to DP/proof-search/hidden terminal SAT?
